text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.49% today, a modest gain that came as oil prices fell sharply—US crude dropped to $107 per barrel and global crude to $130.80—after Saudi Arabia signaled it would release more crude supplies into the market following a pipeline attack. The stock had plunged $8.69 (6.1%) just yesterday, so today's bounce is a partial recovery from that sell-off, not a sign of broader strength.

The backdrop here is mixed geopolitical news: while reports of a potential end to the Iran conflict and Saudi willingness to stabilize supplies eased immediate disruption fears and pressed prices lower, longer-term energy supply could shift with new US policy toward Venezuelan oil development and potential tariffs on countries buying Russian crude. These competing forces—near-term relief in global oil markets offset by uncertainty over policy-driven supply changes—help explain why ConocoPhillips is still down nearly 3% over the past two weeks despite today's small gain.
